data.why: The repo ships no example alignment/tree, so a small synthetic FASTA with date-encoded tip names, a matching Newick tree, and a strain/date CSV (with one missing date) were written to exercise the upload, date-parsing, and tree-viewer steps.

goals: Import a multiple-sequence alignment and confirm taxon count/site length before configuring a model
Assign tip sampling dates (from taxon-name regex or CSV) to enable a time-tree/molecular-clock analysis
Load a starting tree and check root-to-tip regression fits a clock before proceeding
Choose site, substitution, and clock models appropriate for the data (e.g. GTR + strict clock)
Specify a tree prior (e.g. coalescent) and parametric priors on model parameters
Configure the variational-inference (ADVI) algorithm and export a valid torchtree JSON config to run offline

review.summary: The tree captures torchseed's purpose (building a torchtree time-tree/ADVI config the way BEAUti does) with sound phases, faithful labels, and screens that match every node I checked. Before filing it needs the undated/unrooted and protein branches, a real inference-configuration task and feature, and a correction to the order of the date redo so it doesn't imply the exported file had all samples dated.
